![claude-bughunter banner](assets/banner-v2.svg) # claude-bughunter > A self-contained Claude skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work · **85 skills** · 16 slash commands · **681 disclosed-report patterns** (433 now individually cited & auditable) across 24 core vulnerability classes · enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices · engagement-folder scaffolding · Burp MCP integration · battle-tested across authorized red-team and bug-hunting engagements, plus public training platforms (DVWA, OWASP Juice Shop, Hacker101, testphp.vulnweb.com). Built by **[Sachin Sharma](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sachinsharma8080/)** — Bug Hunting & GenAI Security Research.

SPONSORED BY

      

--- ## What is this? `claude-bughunter` is a drop-in skill bundle for the [Claude Code skills system](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills). Install once and Claude Code stops being a chatbot and starts behaving like a senior bug-hunting researcher or red-team operator: it knows the techniques, the chain templates, the VRT mappings, the platform CVE chains, and the hygiene — and it stays in scope. Four layers stack: - **Think** — `bb-methodology` + `redteam-mindset`: the 5-phase non-linear workflow, critical-thinking framework, and red-team operator discipline. - **Hunt webapps** — 58 `hunt-*` skills curated from 681 disclosed HackerOne reports: per-class detection patterns, payloads, bypass tables, and chain templates. - **Hit the perimeter** — enterprise platform chains (M365/Entra, Okta, vCenter, SSL-VPN appliances, SharePoint, cloud IAM): current 2024–2026 CVE chains + post-credential escalation. - **Ship it** — `triage-validation` + reporting + `evidence-hygiene`: the 7-Question Gate, VRT-aware severity, OOS rebuttals, PII redaction, and red-team deliverables. All triggered automatically by topic — describe what you're testing in plain English and the relevant skill loads. No invocation by name. --- ## Quickstart **Option A — install as a Claude Code plugin (recommended).** From inside Claude Code: ```text /plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter /plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls ``` All 85 skills + 16 commands load namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` and update when you bump the plugin version — no files copied into `~/.claude/`. **A HackerOne account is optional.** The install asks for a HackerOne API username and token. They only let the HackerOne MCP read your private programs and your own reports; leave both blank if you don't need that. Every skill, command and the MCP's public tools (duplicate search, program scope) work without them. **Option B — copy install (no plugin system / pin to a clone):** ```bash git clone https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter.git cd Claude-BugHunter ``` ```bash # macOS / Linux bash scripts/install.sh # Windows (PowerShell) pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1 ``` Both copy the skills + commands into `~/.claude/` (macOS/Linux) or `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\` (Windows) and wire the `hunt` engagement scaffolder. **What each install path gives you:** | Path | 85 skills + 16 slash commands | `cbh` CLI | `hunt` scaffolder | |---|---|---|---| | **A — plugin** | ✅ namespaced under `claude-bughunter:` | ➕ separate `pipx install` | ❌ clone-only | | **B — copy install** | ✅ copied into `~/.claude/` | ✅ from the clone | ✅ from the clone | The plugin is the fastest path to the skills + slash commands. The terminal-native `cbh` runner installs standalone — `pipx install claude-bughunter` (or `pipx install git+https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter` for the tip of main) — so plugin users can add it without a full clone (see [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md)). The `hunt` engagement scaffolder ships with the clone (Option B). That's it. Open Claude Code and describe what you're testing in plain English — the right skill loads automatically, no invocation by name: ```text > Testing acme.com — an in-scope HackerOne target. Run recon and rank the surface. ⟳ loading skills: web2-recon, offensive-osint, bb-methodology … → subdomain enum (subfinder + crt.sh) … 47 hosts → live hosts (httpx) … 12 · tech fingerprint … 6 distinct stacks → ranked surface: api.acme.com (GraphQL, introspection ON) ← start here auth.acme.com (OAuth, SSO) ← hunt-oauth Next: want me to probe the GraphQL introspection + OAuth redirect_uri? ``` → Full [Installation guide](INSTALL.md) · [Usage guide](USAGE.md) · [searchable skill catalog](docs/skills.md). > The block above is an illustrative transcript. To record a real demo of your own session: `asciinema rec demo.cast` → upload to [asciinema.org](https://asciinema.org) and drop the badge here. --- ## Runs on multiple agent harnesses ![One install, agent harnesses — Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex CLI, Hermes Agent, Google AntiGravity](assets/harness-routing.svg) The skills are plain [Agent Skills](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/skills) — the same `SKILL.md` format that **Claude Code · OpenCode · OpenAI Codex CLI · Hermes Agent · Google AntiGravity** all load. One command installs them everywhere: ```bash # macOS / Linux bash scripts/install.sh --all --burp-mcp # Windows (PowerShell) pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1 -All -BurpMcp ``` | Harness | Target Skill Directory | Flag | |---|---|---| | **Claude Code** (baseline) | `~/.claude/skills/` | *(default)* | | **OpenCode** | reads `~/.claude/skills/` & `~/.agents/skills/` | *(default)* / `--agents` | | **OpenAI Codex CLI** | `~/.agents/skills/` | `--agents` | | **Hermes Agent** | `~/.hermes/skills/` | `--hermes` | | **Google AntiGravity** | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | `--antigravity` | `--all` (`-All`) detects installed harnesses and copies skills to each harness's path (`~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.hermes/skills`, `~/.gemini/config/skills`); `--burp-mcp` (`-BurpMcp`) wires the Burp MCP server into each. The full *knowledge* layer ports to all five — the slash commands and `/hunt` engine stay Claude-Code-only by design. → [Multi-harness guide](docs/multi-harness.md) --- ## Star History Chart is self-hosted — regenerate with `python3 scripts/gen_star_history.py` (needs `gh auth login`). Refreshes automatically each day via `.github/workflows/star-history.yml`. --- ## Scope — what this bundle is for, and what it isn't This bundle covers the **external attack surface** — anything reachable from the internet without first compromising an internal endpoint. ### In scope - **Bug bounty hunting** — web apps, APIs, SaaS, GraphQL, OAuth, JWT, file upload, IDOR, SSRF, RCE chains - **Web application pentesting** — full hunt-* coverage of OWASP-mapped bug classes + discipline rules - **External red-team engagements** — initial-access against internet-facing enterprise estate: M365 / Entra ID, Okta-as-IdP, SharePoint on-prem (ToolShell + legacy SOAP), VMware vCenter / Workspace ONE, SSL VPN appliances (Cisco / Fortinet / Citrix / Palo Alto / Pulse / SonicWall / F5), Android APK red-team, supply-chain recon - **Cloud misconfig + post-credential escalation** — public S3, IMDS chains, STS AssumeRole, cross-account confused-deputy - **Recon + OSINT** — subdomain enum, identity-fabric mapping, certificate transparency, JS analysis, secret scanning - **Reporting** — H1, Bugcrowd (VRT-aware), Intigriti, Immunefi, plus client-facing red-team deliverable format ### Out of scope (deliberate — not gaps, design decisions) - **Internal Active Directory attacks** — BloodHound, Kerberoasting, ASREProast, DCSync, Pass-the-Hash, AD CS abuse, ntlmrelayx, Responder, PetitPotam, etc. Different operational risk profile; needs different tooling and judgment. **Future bundle, not this one.** - **C2 frameworks** — Cobalt Strike, Sliver, Mythic, Havoc, BRC4 tradecraft. Out of scope for external-only engagement model. - **Post-exploit / persistence / lateral** — Mimikatz/comsvcs LSASS dumping, golden/silver tickets, named-pipe impersonation, persistence (registry, scheduled tasks, WMI events, COM hijacking), token theft. These start after the perimeter has already broken — different bundle territory. - **Evasion** — AMSI bypass, ETW patching, AV/EDR bypass. Tied to C2 tradecraft above. - **iOS pentesting / hardware / RF / ICS** — out of scope by design. - **Binary exploitation / kernel pwn / browser internals** — different skill universe. If you're running an internal red team that includes domain-takeover chains via Kerberos or lateral movement, **this bundle won't help you in those phases** — and we'd rather say that up front than have you find out mid-engagement. The external surface handoff to internal-RT tooling (Impacket, NetExec, CrackMapExec, Rubeus, Certify, BloodHound) is intentionally outside our scope. **Coverage for internal AD and post-exploit may come in a future update.** --- ## What's inside **85 skills**, auto-loaded by topic — no invocation by name. Coverage across the external attack surface: | Category | # | Examples | |---|---|---| | Hunt — web app vuln classes | 58 | XSS, SQLi, SSRF, IDOR, LFI, SSTI, XXE, CSRF, CORS, open-redirect, SharePoint, ASP.NET/NTLM | | Enterprise platform attack ★ | 10 | M365/Entra, Okta, cloud-IAM-deep, vCenter, enterprise VPN, APK/iOS red-team pipelines, supply-chain recon | | Reporting & validation | 7 | triage-validation, evidence-hygiene, report-writing, bugcrowd-reporting | | Recon & OSINT | 5 | web2-recon, offensive-osint, osint-methodology, recon-scope-triage | | Methodology & mindset | 5 | bb-methodology, bug-bounty, redteam-mindset, bb-local-toolkit | Full searchable catalog → **[docs/skills.md](docs/skills.md)**. Also ships **16 slash commands** (`/hunt`, `/recon`, `/report`, …) and a deterministic **engagement engine** (`engine/`) that maps a target's attack surface and routes each finding to the skill that handles it. --- ## How it works A 6-phase, non-linear workflow — **recon → map & rank → hunt → validate → report** — with scope enforced in code and a **7-Question Gate** before anything is submitted. Two ways to drive it: - **Plain English** — describe what you're testing and the relevant skill loads automatically. - **`/hunt` scaffold + `cbh` CLI** — engagement-folder structure, state, and orchestration. → [Usage guide & worked example](USAGE.md) · [6-phase architecture & skill-to-phase map](docs/architecture.md) · [`cbh` CLI](docs/cbh-cli.md) --- ## Authorization These skills are intended for assets you **own** or have **written authorization to assess** (bug-bounty in-scope assets, pentest engagement letters, CTF challenges, your own infrastructure). # /last30days English | [Français](README.fr.md) | [Deutsch](README.de.md) | [Español](README.es.md) | [Português (Brasil)](README.pt-BR.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [العربية](README.ar.md) | [فارسی](README.fa.md) | [Türkçe](README.tr.md) | [Tiếng Việt](README.vi.md) | [Русский](README.ru.md)



**An AI agent-led search engine scored by upvotes, likes, and real money - not editors.** This README tracks the current v4 pipeline. The runtime skill spec lives in [skills/last30days/SKILL.md](skills/last30days/SKILL.md), which is the source of truth for the latest command and setup behavior. **Claude Code (recommended — auto-updates via marketplace):** ``` /plugin marketplace add mvanhorn/last30days-skill /plugin install last30days ``` **Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, or any of 50+ [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) hosts:** ``` npx skills add mvanhorn/last30days-skill -g ``` (`-g` installs globally for your user, available across all projects. Drop it to scope per-project.) More install options (claude.ai web, OpenClaw, manual) in the [Install](#install) section below. Zero config. Reddit, HN, Polymarket, and GitHub work immediately, and so do patent filings and careers pages when your topic is a company. Run it once and the setup wizard unlocks X, YouTube, TikTok, arXiv, Techmeme, and more in 30 seconds. --- Reddit upvotes. X likes. YouTube transcripts. TikTok engagement. Polymarket odds backed by real money and insider information. That's millions of people voting with their attention and their wallets every day. /last30days searches all of it in parallel, scores it by what real people actually engage with, and an AI agent judge synthesizes it into one brief. Google aggregates editors. /last30days searches people. You can't get this search anywhere else because no single AI has access to all of it. Google search doesn't touch Reddit comments or X posts. ChatGPT has a deal with Reddit but can't search X or TikTok. Gemini has YouTube but not Reddit. Claude has none of them natively. Each platform is a walled garden with its own API, its own tokens, its own auth. But you can bring your own keys and browser sessions, and suddenly an AI agent can search all of them at once, score them against each other, and tell you what actually matters. That's the unlock. Not one better search engine. A dozen disconnected platforms, bridged by an agent. ``` /last30days Peter Steinberger ``` You have a meeting tomorrow. You Google them. You get their LinkedIn from 2023. /last30days gives you what they're actually doing this month: joined OpenAI to work on Codex, fighting Anthropic's ban on third-party agents, shipping 23 PRs at 85% merge rate, building "LobsterOS" for cross-device agent control, and r/ClaudeCode hit 569 upvotes debating whether he's a hero or "insufferable." Scattered across X posts, Reddit threads, YouTube transcripts, and GitHub commits. None of it was on Google. ## Why this exists I built it to keep up in AI. Everything changes every day and the Reddit and X nerds are always on top of it first. I needed better prompts, and the training data was always months behind what the community had already figured out. But it turned into something bigger. Now I run it before a sales call to know the last 30 days truth about a business. Before a meeting to read someone's recent tweets and podcast transcripts. Before a Disney World trip to know which rides are closed and what the community says about Genie+. Before I build anything to know what problems people are actually hitting. If you're meeting with a CEO, have you read all their tweets and YouTube transcripts from the last 30 days? I have. ## Sources, scored by the people | Source | What the people tell you | |--------|--------------------------| | **Reddit** | The unfiltered take. Top comments with real upvote counts, free, no API key. The real opinions that Google buries. With your OK, it can also search as your own logged-in Reddit account for more threads and live scores. | | **X / Twitter** | The hot take, the expert thread, the breaking reaction. First to know, first to argue. | | **YouTube** | The 45-minute deep dive. Full transcripts searched for the 5 quotable sentences that matter. | | **TikTok** | The creator reaching 3.6M people with a take you'll never find on Google. | | **Instagram Reels** | The influencer perspective with spoken-word transcripts. The visual culture signal. | | **Hacker News** | The developer consensus. 825 points, 899 comments. Where technical people actually argue. | | **Polymarket** | Not opinions. Odds. Backed by real money. 96% confidence on album sales. 4% on an acquisition. The report puts a market's odds on one line under the story it bears on, with how much they moved. | | **GitHub** | For people: PR velocity, top repos by stars, release notes. For topics: issues and discussions. | | **Digg** | Story clusters from every Digg topic (AI, tech, world and business, sports, science, gaming, entertainment), ranked by Digg Score, with attributable inline quotes from X (no X auth required). Auto-enabled when `digg-pp-cli` is on PATH. An older `digg-pp-cli` still works, on AI and tech only and without scores. | | **arXiv** | The papers behind the hype. New research in the window, free, no API key. Auto-enabled when `arxiv-pp-cli` is on PATH (first-run setup installs it). | | **Techmeme** | The tech-news editorial layer, date-windowed to your 30 days. Free, no API key. Auto-enabled when `techmeme-pp-cli` is on PATH (first-run setup installs it). | | **Yahoo Finance** | The market's read on a company. The share-price move over your 30 days, next to the S&P 500 for US listings. Free, no API key. Shows when your topic is a listed company or the person who leads one and `yahoo-finance-pp-cli` is on PATH (first-run setup installs it). | | **LinkedIn** | The professional signal. Posts and articles, with articles weighted as high signal. | | **Meta Ads** | What a brand is paying to say. Live Meta ad creatives launched this month, with copy, promo codes, and spoken transcripts. | | **StockTwits** | Trader sentiment. Auto-activates when your topic is a ticker or crypto. | | **Threads** | The post-Twitter text layer. Conversations from creators and brands. | | **Pinterest** | Visual discovery. Pins, saves, and comments on products and ideas. | | **Xiaohongshu (RED)** | Chinese lifestyle, product, and creator signals. Requested explicitly with `--search xhs` when a logged-in x-mcp browser plugin or `xiaohongshu-mcp` service is running locally. | | **Bluesky** | The decentralized social layer. AT Protocol posts from the post-Twitter migration. | | **Perplexity** | Controlled Agent API synthesis, OpenRouter Sonar fallback, raw Search API rows, and explicit Deep Research. | | **DEV Community (dev.to)** | Developer articles and top comments through the public, keyless API. Opt in with `--devto-tags`, `--search devto`, or `INCLUDE_SOURCES=devto`. | | **Truth Social** | Posts searched with `TRUTHSOCIAL_TOKEN`; available when authenticated. | | **Telegram** | Public posts from named channels. Opt-in; requires `SCRAPECREATORS_API_KEY` and a channel list. No keyword discovery. | | **Trustpilot** | Company TrustScore, review count, and an AI summary of customer feedback. Opt-in; requires `trustpilot-pp-cli` on PATH and a usable session. | | **Amazon** | Product ratings, prices, and customer reviews. Opt-in; requires an authenticated `brightdata` CLI and uses your Bright Data credits. | | **DripStack** | Financial newsletters and analyst writeups through a public, keyless API. Opt in with `--search dripstack` or `INCLUDE_SOURCES=dripstack`. | | **Jobs / careers pages** | What a company is hiring for, read from its own careers page (Workday, Apple, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Netflix, Oracle, and more). A company run reads it automatically, and roles that hint at something unannounced become Jobs Page Secret Signals. Also selected with `--hiring-signals`, `--search jobs`, or the research plan. | | **Patents** | A company's new US patent filings, as evidence of what it is building before it ships. Free, no API key. Shows when your topic is a company. A filing becomes a Patent Secret Signal only when it is out of character for the company or describes something it has not shipped or announced. | | **Local corpus** | Your local Markdown and text files, plus PDFs when `pdftotext` is on PATH. Opt in with `--corpus` or `LAST30DAYS_CORPUS_DIRS`. | | **Web** | The editorial coverage, the blog comparisons. One signal of many, not the only one. | Ask `/last30days` to include the sources you need. Availability depends on credentials, installed tools, the topic, and explicit opt-ins. See [source requirements](CONFIGURATION.md#source-requirements) for configuration. A Reddit thread with 1,500 upvotes is a stronger signal than a blog post nobody read. A TikTok with 3.6M views tells you more about what's culturally relevant than a press release. Polymarket odds backed by $66K in volume are harder to argue with than a pundit's guess. The synthesis ranks by what real people actually engaged with. Social relevancy, not SEO relevancy. ## What people actually use it for **Before a meeting.** `/last30days Peter Steinberger` - joined OpenAI's Codex team, fighting Anthropic's ban on third-party agents, 23 PRs merged at 85% merge rate on GitHub, building LobsterOS for cross-device agent control. r/ClaudeCode: "Ever since OpenClaw released, it was widely known that if you run it through anything other than the API, you were gonna get banned eventually" (227 upvotes). That's not on LinkedIn. **To see what a company is building before it ships.** `/last30days Apple` - the Jobs Page Secret Signal flagged a new director role testing whether requests trigger transactions that run through partner APIs and financial systems, which reads like quality control for an assistant that completes purchases. The Patent Secret Signal flagged an application for changing a device's state by tapping it in a saved photo of your room. Polymarket put Apple at 91% to be the world's largest company at year end. `/last30days Alphabet` found a product manager role for "YouTube Ads Agentic Buyflows", and its stock line read down 17.6% over 30 days while the S&P 500 fell 3.6%, with the worst day on Oct 29 (-12.6%). For a hiring-only report, add `--hiring-signals`. **To find the topic before it peaks.** Ask `/last30days what's exploding in AI agents?` and the skill switches to discovery mode: the engine sweeps Reddit category listings, Hacker News front/best stories, Digg stories, and X when authenticated; your agent judges the nominations (names, junk filtering, content-worthiness) and writes podcast / X-article angles; then you get 5-10 velocity-ranked topics. Every result includes cross-source numbers, a momentum label, and a ready-to-run `/last30days ""` follow-up. **When something drops.** `/last30days Kanye West` - UK blocked his visa, Wireless Festival canceled, sponsors fled. Give your coding agent a video editor.
Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client edits your footage with local FFmpeg, then checks its own output.
No cloud · No API keys · Python standard library
What you install and what it touches

Website · Quick start · Demos · Tools · MCP · npm

 

 

English · 日本語（サイト）

```bash npx ffmpeg-skill ```

caption.py --animate pop --karaoke
fit.py --aspect 9:16 --fit crop

silence.py --threshold -35
loudness.py -I -14 --tp -1


Twelve clips edited by asking: colour, slow motion and reframing, a talk laid out with its slides and cut into a captioned short, a pause removed, a green-screen composite, a levelled horizon, and three phone clips (stabilised, a night shot lifted and denoised, 60 fps slowed down). Watch them (English and Japanese) · the request and the exact commands. Nine clips are AI-generated with Google Veo; three are shot on a phone.

### Review page After an edit, ask your agent for the review page ("show me the review page"), or run `npx ffmpeg-skill review project.json --result run.json` yourself (`python3 scripts/_review.py` from a checkout). It writes one local HTML file. It shows the sources, every step with its checks, the result in a phone frame with the platform's safe area, and a timeline. Press the number of a clip or a caption, write what should change, and copy the instruction it builds back to your agent. Nothing is uploaded; the page speaks English, Japanese, Korean and Chinese.


The talk above as a vertical short, on the review page (AI-generated footage).

Left half is the input, right half is what the command produced. **[Every before/after demo, with the exact command under each one →](docs/demos.md)** — all of it built by `python3 demos/build.py`, so you can rebuild every frame of it yourself. The pictures come from [demos/footage/](demos/footage/README.md): clips AI-generated with Google Veo (the people and places do not exist) and a few shot on a phone. The sound is synthetic, and a few demos (HDR10, a panorama) use a synthetic picture. `ffmpeg-skill` is an [Agent Skill](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/agent-skills) for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and any agent that reads `SKILL.md`. It teaches the agent a fixed workflow (probe → edit losslessly where possible → check → verify) and ships **42 tools** that do the actual work with `ffmpeg` / `ffprobe`: cut, join, silence removal, fit to duration and aspect, captions and karaoke, overlays and motion graphics, HDR → SDR and LUTs, audio clean-up and typed dynamics, sync with drift correction, multicam, loudness, delivery checks, whole-edit project rendering, batch folders. Every tool is also callable as an MCP tool (`tools/list` advertises a core 12 by default to keep client context small, with `FFMPEG_SKILL_MCP_FULL=1` listing all 42; every tool is reachable by name through `tools/call` either way), and the whole set is described by a machine-readable contract. If `ffmpeg` and `python3` are on your PATH, it works: offline, on footage you would rather not upload. - **Protect your source files.** A destination that matches a declared input is refused. Direct edits require `--overwrite` to replace an existing output. A `batch --watch` job can replace an unchanged file it delivered on an earlier pass. The `-y` in the dry-run command takes effect only after the tool checks the destination. - **Call typed tools.** The agent supplies named options such as `--aspect 9:16` and `--fit pad`. The tool builds the FFmpeg command and filter graph. - **Verify the edit.** The tools probe the source and the written file, so the agent can check the actual duration, frame size and audio before reporting success. > **SPEC** (Self-Producing Execution Contract): each tool's `input_schema` — the part of its > contract and MCP tool definition that has to track the CLI flag-for-flag — is never > hand-authored beside the code. It is derived, at run time, from the same `argparse` parser that > already defines the CLI, and CI fails the build if any of it drifts. > → [full explanation](#what-is-spec) --- ## Standalone, and in an ecosystem **Standalone**, this is a local FFmpeg engine: probe → edit → verify, `npx ffmpeg-skill` and nothing else. No API key, no account, no other repo required. Everything above and below this section describes that standalone tool, and none of it changes if you never read the rest of this one. **In [kajisho5](https://github.com/kajisho5)'s wider video-production ecosystem**, this repo is the *hands*: it cuts, measures and exports files, and reports back in structured JSON. It does not decide what to cut, whether a deliverable is approvable, what makes a highlight interesting, or what a caption should say (the user's cue text is burned as written, never rewritten to fit) — those are a *brain*'s job, sitting in front of this engine, not inside it. | You want to... | Use | |---|---| | Cut / join / measure / export a file right now | **this repo** (`ffmpeg-skill`), standalone | | Decide cut points, approve a deliverable, plan a whole edit | [`video-production-agent`](https://github.com/kajisho5/video-production-agent) / [`AI-video-production-OS`](https://github.com/kajisho5/AI-video-production-OS) | | Build a typed editing graph across a workspace, without writing raw `ffmpeg` | [`video-editing-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/video-editing-skill) / [`audio-production-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/audio-production-skill) | | Put Remotion motion graphics (animated captions, silence jump cuts, audio-peak motion) on a real recording | [`remotion-ffmpeg-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/remotion-ffmpeg-skill): its compositions take their length, fps, frame, silences, scene cuts, audio peaks and beats from this repo's `probe.py`, `silence.py` and `scenes.py`. It verifies its render with `check.py` and `look.py`, composites a graphics layer with `overlay.py` (`--place` for its `--sparse` mode), and delivers through `render.py --template` | Other repos in the ecosystem — [`media-analysis-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/media-analysis-skill), [`transcription-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/transcription-skill), [`subtitle-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/subtitle-skill), [`thumbnail-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/thumbnail-skill), [`color-grading-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/color-grading-skill), [`motion-graphics-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/motion-graphics-skill), [`qc-skill`](https://github.com/kajisho5/qc-skill) — read this repo's `contract --json`, its tools' `--json` output and `doctor`, the same way any agent framework would; this repo does not call into any of them. The dependency runs one way. --- **Contents** [Standalone, and in an ecosystem](#standalone-and-in-an-ecosystem) · [Why](#why) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Design principles](#design-principles) · [Tools](#tools) · [Audio](#audio-is-a-first-class-input) · [Built for agents](#built-for-agents) · [FAQ](#faq) · [FFmpeg compatibility](#ffmpeg-compatibility) · [Tested on real footage](#tested-on-real-footage) · [Install](#install) · [Requirements](#requirements) · [Development](#development) · [Docs](#docs) --- ## Why An agent that "knows FFmpeg" still guesses: it assumes a frame rate, picks a codec the container cannot hold, re-encodes a file that only needed a stream copy, and reports "done" without opening the result. This skill takes the guessing out: - **Real files first.** Every job starts with `probe.py`; the agent decides from the measured duration, fps, resolution, colour and audio layout, not from the file name. - **Structured tools, not shell strings.** Each operation is a script with typed arguments. Nothing runs through a shell; no filter graph is accepted from the caller. - **A contract the agent can read.

Each model runtime and resource pack is downloaded and uninstalled independently inside the app, sharing the same voice library, audio export, QQ voice sending, and local HTTP API. | Model | Status | Highlights | |---|---|---| | [GPT-SoVITS](https://github.com/RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS) | ✅ Supported | V2 Pro, V2 Pro Plus, and V5 Turbo; cross-lingual cloning and on-device `.ckpt` / `.pth` conversion | | [Ming-TTS 0.5B](https://github.com/inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts) | ✅ Supported | 93 built-in official voices, single-clip cloning, emotion and dialect controls, reading instructions, and streaming playback | | [CosyVoice3-0.5B-2512](https://github.com/FunAudioLLM/CosyVoice) | 🔧 Inference Ready | Mobile inference verified; app integration pending | | [Qwen3-TTS-0.6B-Base](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS) | 🔧 Inference Ready | Mobile inference verified; app integration pending | | [IndexTTS-2.5](https://github.com/index-tts/index-tts) | 🗺️ Planned | Planned for mobile support | | [Fish Audio S1-mini](https://github.com/fishaudio/fish-speech) | 🗺️ Planned | Planned for mobile support | | [OmniVoice](https://github.com/k2-fsa/OmniVoice) | 🗺️ Planned | Planned for mobile support | ## Features - **On-demand model packs**: The app and inference backends are decoupled. Download, verify, or uninstall individual model runtimes and packs on demand inside the app without bloating the APK. - **Offline inference with hardware acceleration**: Everything runs locally once models are ready, with no network calls or cloud GPUs. Built for GPU-accelerated mobile devices, with additional Qualcomm QNN NPU hybrid acceleration on compatible Snapdragon phones. - **Zero-shot cloning and expressive controls**: GPT-SoVITS supports cross-lingual voice transfer and direct on-device import of native `.ckpt` and `.pth` checkpoints; Ming-TTS 0.5B includes 93 official voices, single-clip cloning, speed/pitch/volume controls, emotions, dialects, natural-language reading instructions, and real-time streaming playback. - **Native QQ voice messages**: Send generated audio directly as native, tap-to-play QQ voice messages rather than audio attachments. [Watch QQ demo](https://github.com/Renakoni/Voicebox/blob/main/.github/assets/demo-qq.mp4) - **Local HTTP API**: Lightweight `127.0.0.1` server for audiobook readers, Tasker, or other clients, with desktop access supported via ADB port forwarding. - **Verified in-app updates**: Check GitHub for new releases inside the app, with automatic verification of file size, SHA-256, package name, and version. ## Getting Started Download **Voicebox 1.2.0** from [Releases](https://github.com/Renakoni/Voicebox/releases/latest) (requires an ARM64 device running Android 11 or later). > [!WARNING] > 1.2.0 is a breaking release and cannot be installed over earlier versions. Uninstall any previous version before installing 1.2.0 (future releases will update in place). 1. **Install models**: Open **Models** and install **GPT-SoVITS** or **Ming-TTS 0.5B** as needed. 2. **Set up voices**: Open **Voices** to pick an official voice, or record/import a reference clip with its transcript to clone a voice. For GPT-SoVITS, you can also import local `.ckpt` and `.pth` weights directly. 3. **Create and export**: Open **Create**, pick a voice and adjust your settings, enter text, and generate. Play, save, share, or send the result to QQ.
One-time setup for QQ voice messages 1. Turn on **Wireless debugging** in Android's Developer options. 2. On the **Send to QQ** screen, tap **Connect** and enter the six-digit pairing code shown by Android. Pairing is only needed once. 3. Tap **Choose contact and send**, then open the target chat in QQ. Voicebox will record a placeholder voice message, replace its audio, and send it. Leave QQ untouched until it finishes. Each message must be shorter than 60 seconds.
## Performance and Quality All mobile benchmarks were measured on a **Xiaomi 14 (Snapdragon 8 Gen 3, 16 GB RAM)** using the same Chinese short sentence (~3.5–4 s) and long passage (~19–22 s), with official weights or fixed presets and seeds. Once models and caches were warm, each configuration and length ran **10 times** at normal ambient temperature with no thermal throttling; values are reported as **mean ± standard deviation**. | Model | Execution Path | Short RTF | Long RTF | ASR Agreement | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | GPT-SoVITS V2 Pro Plus | GPU | 0.614 | 0.556 | 99.34% | | GPT-SoVITS V2 Pro Plus | GPU + NPU | 0.627 | 0.511 | 99.72% | | GPT-SoVITS V5 Turbo | GPU | 2.038 | 1.816 | 99.72% | | GPT-SoVITS V5 Turbo | GPU + NPU | 1.313 | 0.954 | 99.62% | | Ming-TTS 0.5B | GPU | 1.821 | 1.055 | 100.00% / 100.00% | | Ming-TTS 0.5B | GPU + NPU | 1.599 | 0.574 | 100.00% / 99.89% | - **RTF (Real-Time Factor)**: Inference time ÷ audio duration. Values below `1.0` run faster than real-time playback. - **ASR agreement**: Transcribed offline with SenseVoice and scored after stripping punctuation as `(1 − character edit distance ÷ reference length) × 100%`. For Ming-TTS 0.5B, values show short / long results respectively. - **Execution paths**: GPU runs on CPU + WebGPU; GPU + NPU adds Qualcomm QNN heterogeneous acceleration.
GPT-SoVITS detailed benchmarks #### 1. Mobile vs. desktop GPU latency The desktop baseline runs the [official repository](https://github.com/RVC-Boss/GPT-SoVITS) CUDA implementation on an RTX 3070 Ti Laptop (8 GB VRAM, 16 GB RAM), using official weights and the same Chinese reference clip (~4 s short sentence, ~22 s long passage). | Model | Implementation / Device | Short time (s) | Short RTF | Long time (s) | Long RTF | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | V2 Pro Plus | GPT-SoVITS · RTX 3070 Ti Laptop | 1.380 ± 0.382 | 0.341 ± 0.089 | 6.153 ± 0.301 | 0.265 ± 0.007 | | V2 Pro Plus | Voicebox · GPU | 2.587 ± 0.182 | 0.614 ± 0.043 | 12.637 ± 0.453 | 0.556 ± 0.005 | | V2 Pro Plus | Voicebox · GPU + NPU | 2.618 ± 0.927 | 0.627 ± 0.286 | 11.955 ± 0.608 | 0.511 ± 0.007 | | V5 Turbo | GPT-SoVITS · RTX 3070 Ti Laptop | 1.680 ± 0.326 | 0.416 ± 0.086 | 6.217 ± 0.566 | 0.278 ± 0.021 | | V5 Turbo | Voicebox · GPU | 8.173 ± 0.429 | 2.038 ± 0.102 | 40.676 ± 2.589 | 1.816 ± 0.043 | | V5 Turbo | Voicebox · GPU + NPU | 5.367 ± 0.301 | 1.313 ± 0.074 | 21.479 ± 0.867 | 0.954 ± 0.021 | #### 2. Waveform error and transcription accuracy Waveform error compares phone GPU + NPU output against official PyTorch FP32 under identical inputs and noise. SenseVoice transcribed all clips generated in the latency runs. | Model | RMS Short | RMS Long | ASR · Official CUDA | ASR · Phone GPU | ASR · Phone GPU + NPU | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | V2 Pro Plus | 0.2323% | 0.2351% | 99.06% | 99.34% | 99.72% | | V5 Turbo | 1.4489% | 0.6537% | 99.25% | 99.72% | 99.62% | - **Relative RMS error**: `RMS(phone − official) ÷ RMS(official) × 100%`; lower means closer numerical match to FP32. - See [Architecture and Optimizations](docs/METHODS_EN.md) for model analysis and scheduling details.
Ming-TTS 0.5B detailed benchmarks Repeated runs used the official Chinese preset `灵小柔`, outputting 44.1 kHz mono 16-bit PCM WAV. | Execution Path | Passage | Audio Length (s) | End-to-End Time (s) | Inference RTF | ASR Agreement | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | GPU | Short | 3.57 ± 0.11 | 11.88 ± 0.50 | 1.821 ± 0.068 | 100.00% | | GPU | Long | 19.19 ± 0.40 | 25.70 ± 1.03 | 1.055 ± 0.044 | 100.00% | | GPU + NPU | Short | 3.59 ± 0.11 | 11.20 ± 0.42 | 1.599 ± 0.031 | 100.00% | | GPU + NPU | Long | 19.17 ± 0.30 | 16.42 ± 0.52 | 0.574 ± 0.009 | 99.89% | - **NPU speedup**: Accelerating acoustic synthesis via QNN reduces long-passage RTF by **45.5%** and cuts end-to-end latency from 25.70 s to 16.42 s. - **Timing breakdown**: Inference RTF divides core synthesis time by output WAV duration. End-to-end time also includes app preparation, session setup, and WAV export (~5.4 s on long passages). - **Cold start and cache**: Cold short-sentence requests take 12.87 s on GPU. First-time NPU graph compilation takes 17.53 s and caches a ~205 MB QNN context; subsequent runs reuse the cache and drop to 11.39 s. - **Additional checks**: All generated WAV files decoded cleanly with zero clipping; NPU checks for Chinese voice cloning and English presets both reached 100.00% ASR agreement.
## Building from Source Requires JDK 21, Android SDK 37 (with NDK and CMake), and Python 3.12+. ```powershell git clone https://github.com/Renakoni/Voicebox.git cd Voicebox/Android .\gradlew.bat :app:assembleDebug ``` `:app:assembleDebug` builds the app shell, which downloads model runtimes from Releases on demand. To package a WebGPU-enabled GPT-SoVITS backend yourself, build the custom ONNX Runtime ([build script](tools/build_ort_webgpu.ps1), [patches](Android/model/gptsovits/patches)) and pass `-PvoiceboxOrtAar=` when running `:model:gptsovits:bundleDebugBridge` or `:model:gptsovits:bundleReleaseBridge`; omitting it builds a CPU-only backend package. ## Feedback and Contributing [Issues](https://github.com/Renakoni/Voicebox/issues) and [pull requests](https://github.com/Renakoni/Voicebox/pulls) are welcome. When reporting a bug, please include the app version, phone model, TTS mode

# 简体中文 ## 它做什么 你照常玩日文原版，MeguLit 在旁边帮你读 - **点读**：直接点游戏里的词，读音、释义马上出来；拖一段查短语。点了不会推进剧情 - **原文**：直接从游戏里读出正在显示的台词，不截图、不 OCR，字不会认错 - **翻译和注音**：写在原文旁边，不盖住游戏画面。装过汉化补丁的话，直接用汉化组的译文，一句不等 - **AI 讲解**：选中词或整句，让 AI 讲语法和语境 - **声音**：有配音的句子播游戏原声，没配音的才用本地语音 - **学习**：查过的词进生词本，一键做成带截图和原声的 Anki 卡片；零基础可以从五十音和语法课开始 界面有简体中文、English、日本語。主要面向学日语的中文 / 英文用户，反过来用日语学中文或英文也可以 ## 最近更新 | | | |---|---| | **内嵌显示** | 原文、注音、翻译直接画进游戏里，选项按钮也能内嵌。新支持 ファタモルガーナの館（海市蜃楼之馆）、沙耶の唄（沙耶之歌）HD、魔法使いの夜（魔法使之夜）整页、euphoria、穢翼のユースティア（秽翼的尤斯蒂娅）等 | | **游戏原声** | 有配音的句子一律播游戏自己的 CV：CLANNAD、千恋＊万花（千恋万花）、WHITE ALBUM2（白色相簿2）等；Anki 录音自动去掉背景音乐 | | **语法课** | 从 N5 一路到 N0（含 2025–2026 流行语），例句来自你读过的台词 | | **新首页和日报** | 首页重做，自己挑展示的作品；「日报」看 Galgame 新闻和每日热词 | | **零延迟翻译** | 你装过的汉化补丁直接当译文，KiriKiri、BGI、Siglus、YU-RIS、Artemis、Ren'Py 等引擎都能对上；没汉化的句子提前机翻 | | **日文原版恢复** | Steam 中文 / 英文版一键换回日文，也能用日文原版的压缩包、文件夹或光盘镜像对照替换，全部备份、一键还原 | 更早的更新见 [Releases](https://github.com/ilynthn/MeguLit/releases)
## 功能预览 ### 游戏库

每打一个字母，不相关的封面就散开，剩下的排到中间

游戏库 · 扫描文件夹和 Steam，系列作品自动归到一起 作品详情 · 简介、各站评分、阅读记录、关联单词和收藏的句子
1. 第一次打开时选好放游戏的文件夹，MeguLit 会自动找出日文原版 EXE 2. 点封面进入作品详情，点「启动游戏」。需要转区的游戏可以单独开 Locale Emulator 3. 游戏启动后阅读层自动接上，按 Alt + T 呼出菜单 ### 自动更新 - 每次启动都会联网检查一次新版本，有的话直接在后台下载 - 卡片上写着版本号、更新内容，以及安装包比现在大还是小多少 - 下载有真实进度条，下完先校验，再由你选「重启并更新」或「稍后」 - 也可以随时到「关于」页点「检查更新」手动检查 - 只替换程序文件，游戏库、学习记录和设置都会保留 ### 阅读层 两种显示方式，都不抢焦点，点它也不会让剧情往下走 - **内嵌**：原文、注音、翻译直接画进游戏的文本框位置，选项按钮也一样 - **阅读层**：浮在游戏上面，内嵌不了的游戏用它 - **点一下**查单词，**拖一段**查短语，离线词典 - 注音优先用游戏自带的 ruby，没有再用词典和上下文 - 翻译支持 DeepL、Bing、Google、Gemini、DeepSeek、Sakura、Ollama 和 OpenAI 兼容接口，密钥加密存在本地 - 选中词或整句，让 AI 讲语法和语境 - 有配音的句子播游戏原声，没配音的才用本地 TTS - 每部作品单独记字体、颜色和位置 ### 历史
阅读会话 · 每次玩了多久、读了多少字 对话记录 · 读过的每一句原文和译文
### 学习
Anki 复习 · 直接用 Anki 的卡片和调度，评分写回 Anki 单词本 · 查过的词、读音、释义和掌握程度

学习统计 · 阅读字数、时长、查词、日历、每部作品的阅读量、字数走势、阅读时段和星期分布

空页面 · 告诉你这里会出现什么、怎么让它出现 工具 · 日文原版恢复、修复内嵌替换

## 五十音 给零基础的人：先认得每一个假名，再到游戏里把它读出来 **学习 → 五十音 → 开始学习**。主页记住你学到哪一课，右边是平假名熟悉度
一课四步 · 认识 → 辨认 → 回忆 → 混合。笔顺、字源、例词，还有你自己玩过的游戏里含这个假名的台词 五十音图 · 平 / 片假名，清音、浊音、拗音；点格子看笔顺、发音要点和易混字
假名游戏 · 三种玩法、四档难度，规则都写在面板上 行段识别 · 先按辅音字母选行，再按元音选段
结算 · 达成率、判定、答题轨迹和错题分析，一键错题再挑战 学习手帐 · 熟悉度、到期复习（1 → 3 → 7 → 21 天）、个人最佳
玩法、难度和评分规则
| 玩法 | 怎么玩 | |---|---| | 行段识别 | 看到「き」，答出 か行 · い段。键盘先按 k 再按 i | | 前后假名 | 按 あいうえお…わをん 的顺序说出前一个和后一个，空位直接跳过 | | 平片转换 | 看平假名写片假名，反过来也一样。可以用日语输入法（F7 / F6），也可以按 K 打开屏幕假名键盘 | | 难度 | 规则 | |---|---| | 入门 | 只考学过的假名，不限时，每题可看提示 | | 标准 | 全部清音，每题限时，整局 3 次提示 | | 进阶 | 加入浊音、拗音和易混字，限时更短 | | 挑战 | 总计 90 秒，错 3 次结束，没有提示 | - 每道题是一个音符：普通假名算 TAP，最容易认错的几组（シ / ツ、ソ / ン、ぬ / め、ね / れ / わ…）算 **BREAK**，分量是 5 倍 - 答得快是 CRITICAL PERFECT，稍慢 PERFECT，再慢 GREAT；用了提示算 GOOD，答错或超时算 MISS - 基础 100% 加 BREAK 奖励最多 1%，**满分 101.0000%**，评级从 SSS+ 到 D 快捷键：Enter 下一个，Space 发音，← → 切换假名，答题时按 1–4
汉字读音 · 学完假名可以玩《漢字でGO!》。MeguLit 只是在窗口里原样打开 PLiCy 上的官方页面（作者 Micelle，含广告），不是 MeguLit 的一部分；不想在 MeguLit 里玩，可以点「在浏览器打开」

## 安装 > [!IMPORTANT] > **游戏剧情必须是日文原文**。MeguLit 读的是游戏正在显示的台词，剧情被汉化后读到的就不是日文。只汉化了菜单、剧情仍是日文的游戏不受影响；汉化版可以先试试「工具 → 日文原版恢复」 1. 去 [Releases](https://github.com/ilynthn/MeguLit/releases/latest) 下载 `MeguLit-v1.4.25-win-x64.zip`，完整解压后双击 `Install MeguLit.cmd`。确认安装后，安装程序会按需安装包内的微软 Visual C++ x64 运行库 2. 第一次启动会弹出安装窗口，马上开始下载运行组件（约 565 MB，含注音词典和 AivisSpeech 语音引擎，需要约 1.8 GB 空间）。下载的同时选好安装位置和快捷方式，点「安装」，下完自动装好；中途关掉，下次打开会接着下 3. 选好放游戏的文件夹，等游戏库扫描完 4. 点一部作品 →「启动游戏」，**用窗口模式玩** 5. 零基础的话，先去 学习 → 五十音 之后每次启动会自动检查更新，只换程序文件，游戏库、学习记录和设置都保留 需要 Windows 10 / 11 x64 和 Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime
## 常见问题
全屏玩的时候翻译显示不全，或者文字跑到了桌面上
请把游戏切到**窗口模式**。独占全屏下游戏会盖住其他所有窗口，阅读层没法稳定地画在游戏上面。窗口拉大一点也没关系
读到的是乱码，或者根本不是日文
剧情必须是日文原文。汉化版先试试「工具 → 日文原版恢复」；乱码的话在 Alt + T 里重选文本流
更新会不会弄丢我的数据
不会。自动更新只替换程序文件，`data`、`logs`、`cache`、`runtime`、`models` 都不碰。旧的 `MeguLit.exe` 还会留一份 `MeguLit.rollback-update.exe`
Anki 连不上
先打开 Anki，并装好 AnkiConnect（MeguLit 里可以一键安装）。端口 8765 被别的程序占用也会连不上
某个游戏读不到文字
不同引擎差别很大。请在「关于 → 一键上传问题反馈」告诉我们，或者在 [Issues](https://github.com/ilynthn/MeguLit/issues) 留下游戏名
